questions.q: Why does this lesson say environment strategy must be decided before CI/CD pipeline design?
options: Because CI/CD pipelines cannot technically be built in Salesforce
Because a pipeline is built to move changes between environments, so the environments and their purposes have to exist as a deliberate design first
Because sandboxes are more expensive to set up than pipelines
Because environment strategy and CI/CD design are actually the same task
questions.explain: A CI/CD pipeline moves changes between defined environments; without first deciding what those environments are and what each is for, there is nothing concrete for a pipeline to move changes between.

questions.q: Why does LTV Global maintain a dedicated integration sandbox, separate from any single business unit's sandbox?
options: Because integrations run through one shared hub, and a dedicated, separately-owned sandbox catches cross-BU integration conflicts before they reach staging
Because each business unit is legally required to have its own isolated integration environment
Because the integration sandbox replaces the need for a staging environment
Because Meridian ERP requires a dedicated sandbox by technical mandate
questions.explain: Since the integration hub is shared across all four BUs, a dedicated integration sandbox owned by the integration team (not any one BU) is where cross-BU integration changes are tested against each other before reaching staging.

questions.q: What does Salesforce DX treat as the source of truth for metadata, per this lesson?
options: A single long-lived production sandbox
Version control, with metadata as source-driven rather than living inside any one sandbox
The integration sandbox exclusively
Whatever sandbox the most senior developer is currently using
questions.explain: Salesforce DX and source-driven development treat version control as the source of truth for metadata, rather than treating any individual sandbox as authoritative.

questions.q: Why are scratch orgs well suited to LTV Global's four-business-unit development structure?
options: Because scratch orgs are permanent and shared across all BUs
Because a developer can spin up a scratch org scoped to exactly the feature they're working on and tear it down when done, without needing a shared, limited-supply sandbox slot for every small change
Because scratch orgs replace the need for a staging environment entirely
Because scratch orgs automatically merge changes from all four BUs
questions.explain: Scratch orgs are temporary and disposable, letting individual developers work in isolation on exactly the metadata their feature touches without competing for a limited, long-lived sandbox slot.

questions.q: What risk does this lesson identify if Parts & Aftermarket were given its own separate integration sandbox, isolated from the other three BUs?
options: No risk — this is exactly what the lesson recommends
It would undermine testing cross-BU conflicts against the shared integration hub, since a change one BU makes to a shared hub connection could affect every other BU
It would violate GDPR data residency requirements
It would make the staging environment unnecessary
questions.explain: Because the integration hub is shared across all BUs, splitting integration sandboxes per BU would prevent catching conflicts between BUs' changes to the same shared hub connections before they reach staging or production.
